topic.title: The bank we never leave
topic.claim: We will switch phones, apps and jobs, but the salary account stays where HR opened it, and banks know it.
topic.behaviour: Sitting with one bank for years, grumbling about each new charge, and still never moving.
topic.mechanism: Inertia and paperwork dread. The account feels like a household appliance, not a product you shop for. That loyalty is what lets small fees creep in quietly.
real_details: From 1 October SBI salary-package holders get 5 free other-bank ATM transactions a month, down from 10
After that, a cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST
Basic savings accounts pay ₹15 plus GST per withdrawal beyond four a month
From 1 October RBI rules require the same rate on similar deposits accepted the same day at any branch and published rate schedules
Salaried users are complaining about creeping bank charges
topic.news_peg: SBI ATM limit cut and RBI deposit-rate rules, both from 1 October 2026
topic.why_now: Both changes landed together this month and show how much banks rely on us staying put.

score.why: Concrete, plain reframe on how banks profit off our inertia, no company blamed for wrongdoing, just the pattern, like the bestseller-tag take.
